record.context_brief: Total positivity of the Eulerian matrix
record.original_question: Let A(n,k) be the Eulerian number counting permutations in S_n with k descents, and form the infinite matrix A = (A(n+1,k))_{n,k in N}. Is this matrix totally positive?

evidence.quote: For n in P and k in N let A(n,k) be the corresponding Eulerian number (so, A(n,k) is the number of permutations in S_n that have k descents).
Conjecture 2.12. The matrix A := (A(n + 1, k))_{n,k in N} is totally positive.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For positive integers n and nonnegative integers k, let A(n,k) denote the Eulerian number, defined as the number of permutations of {1,2,...,n} having exactly k descents (where a descent of a permutation σ is an index i with σ(i) > σ(i+1)). Form the infinite matrix
  A = (A(n+1, k))_{n,k ∈ N},
indexed by n,k ∈ {0,1,2,...}. The matrix A is called totally positive if every minor (determinant of any finite square submatrix) is nonnegative.

Determine whether the matrix A is totally positive.
artifact.status_search_result: The total positivity of the Eulerian triangle is a longstanding conjecture of Brenti (1996). Recent work (including a December 2024 paper developing planar network techniques for total positivity of combinatorial matrices) explicitly notes that this conjecture remains open, while proving total positivity for related matrices such as reversed Stirling triangles of the second kind, Lah numbers, and derangements.

status_evidence.title: A unified planar network approach to total positivity of combinatorial matrices and real-rootedness of polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Although the total positivity of the Eulerian triangle is hard to prove, ... the total positivity of the reversal of the Stirling triangle of the second kind.
status_evidence.claim: Brenti's conjecture on total positivity of the Eulerian triangle remains an open problem; recent planar network techniques have not resolved it.

status_evidence.title: A008292 - OEIS (Eulerian numbers)
status_evidence.snippet: Eulerian numbers (Euler's triangle: column k of triangle of Eulerian numbers T(n,k)).
status_evidence.claim: Standard definition of Eulerian numbers A(n,k) counting permutations of [n] with k descents.
